title: Push the landed commit for land --pr and repair open PRs on rerun
summary: Choose and record an approach so every commit on athena/<job> passes `athena check --history`; the proposed one is pushing the job's locally landed commit (from the outcome record) instead of the bare candidate or a synthetic records commit. Rerunning `land --pr` on a job with an open PR replaces the branch head with that commit (forced, safely, since the branch is Athena's own) and reuses the PR, which repairs PR #39 on job b67z.

defaults_applied.how: All changes are Rust and Markdown docs.
New tests for the pushed commit and rerun repair; cargo test and clippy must pass.
The approach choice and alternatives are written down in the design doc.
One focused change to the PR publish path.
Behavior verified by running the tests.
The push guard enforces the branch restriction in code, tested.

assumptions: The push uses the landed commit in the job's outcome record (landed_commit), or the commit on local HEAD carrying that job's Athena-Job trailer, so each pushed commit has trailers and records.
Replacing the head uses a lease-protected force push (--force-with-lease against the observed remote head), limited to athena/<job> by the existing push guard.
The PR stays reused: the stored link is kept and its head updated; no second PR is opened.
The decision and its alternatives (bare candidate plus trailer rewrite, synthetic records commit, landed commit) are recorded in docs/design/native-pr-landing.md and/or docs/decisions.md.
Merging stays behind the off-by-default merge_via_rest opt-in.

acceptance_criteria.text: The pushed head for athena/<job> is the job's locally landed commit (with its Athena-Job trailer and records), not the bare candidate nor the records-only commit made by work_commit/commit_with_records; the unused code is removed or justified.
The chosen approach, rejected alternatives, and the reason (every pushed commit must pass athena check --history alone) are recorded in the design doc or decisions.md, and CHANGELOG.md is updated.

When a stored PR link is open and the remote branch head differs from the fixed commit, land_pr replaces the branch head (guarded to athena/<job> only, with a lease) and reuses the same PR number, updating the stored link head; it does not open a second PR.
The push guard still refuses any branch other than athena/<job> and any force outside the replace path.

Run `cargo test`: new unit tests in gh.rs (fake remote and host) cover the pushed commit being the landed one, rerun with an open PR replacing the head and not calling open_pr, rerun when the head already matches (no-op), and refusal for non-work branches; an athena-git test covers the lease force push.
Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: all pass with no warnings.
A test using a real temporary git repo with a bare remote shows the pushed branch's commits each pass the history check (trailer on governed and records changes), run via `cargo test`.

out_of_scope: Actually repairing PR #39 on GitHub (the user reruns athena land --pr afterward).
Changing CI workflows or athena check --history itself.
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass odds than the reference: the change spans the push guard, a force push, rerun semantics and a design record, with several test layers.
